---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Horizon-Matched Build Minus Buy with Claims-Coverage Floor
EXPRESSION: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), TS_SUM(DELTA(ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), COALESCE(intan, 0)), 1), 5)), at)), IND_RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(oancf, lct), 5)))
HYPOTHESIS: Durable intangible productivity is a firm that spent five years building knowledge rather than buying it, and whose worst-year cash flow still covered the claims actually falling due, so the enabling condition is solvency against obligations rather than a return on an arbitrary asset base.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The archive's two best components have never been paired: the horizon-matched build-minus-buy leg carries the highest cross-sectional slope in the archive (fmb 5.86 with alpha 4.4%) and the claims-coverage floor the highest among floor variants (fmb 4.94 with alpha 4.9%), and each was tested against the other theme's weaker partner. The denominator is current liabilities alone, correcting the double counting of short-term debt in the original coverage construct, so this is the cleanest statement of the mechanism the whole run has converged on.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Intangible Allocation Per Dollar of Business Scale
EXPRESSION: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), TS_SUM(DELTA(ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), COALESCE(intan, 0)), 1), 5)), MA(revt, 3))), IND_RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(ADD(ib, dp), at), 5)))
HYPOTHESIS: The build-versus-buy allocation should be judged against the size of the business it serves, not against the asset base, because asset scaling mechanically favours asset-light firms and conflates the intangible allocation decision with capital intensity.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Every intangibles leg in the archive is scaled by assets, so the recurring result could partly reflect an asset-light tilt rather than an allocation choice; revenue scaling breaks that link while leaving the economic content — five years of research spending net of five years of purchased-intangible additions — unchanged. Paired with the income-statement cash-earnings floor it also runs at roughly 0.13 coverage rather than 0.084, so a comparable alpha would show the effect is neither an asset-scaling artefact nor a post-1988 sample artefact.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Profit-Funded Knowledge Stock
EXPRESSION: IND_RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(MUL(COALESCE(xrd, 0), INDICATOR(ib, 0)), 5), at))
HYPOTHESIS: Research dollars spent in profitable years are credible investment; research dollars spent in loss years are subsidised experimentation, so the priced knowledge stock is the cumulative research a firm financed while actually earning money, not its total research spending.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This puts the quality-intangibles interaction inside the accumulation itself — each year's research is admitted to the stock only if that year's earnings were positive — rather than conjoining a research measure with a separate profitability screen, which is a construction the archive has never used and which cannot be produced by ranking R&D intensity and profitability separately. It is a single continuous leg with no rank splice, computable for the full sample at roughly 0.145 coverage, and the smooth form is the one that has generated the archive's highest FF5 t-statistics.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Profit-Funded Knowledge Net of Deal Outlays
EXPRESSION: IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(TS_SUM(MUL(COALESCE(xrd, 0), INDICATOR(ib, 0)), 5), TS_SUM(DELTA(ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), COALESCE(intan, 0)), 1), 5)), at))
HYPOTHESIS: Over any five-year window a firm either compounds knowledge out of its own profits or buys intangible assets from outside, and the net of these two same-horizon dollar flows is the single number that identifies durable intangible productivity without needing a separate quality screen.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The earnings condition is embedded in the numerator's accumulation and the acquisitiveness penalty in its subtraction, so the whole mechanism sits in one continuous variable — the functional form that produced ls_talpha 4.51 and 4.77 in the archive — while avoiding the MIN kink that flattens Fama-MacBeth slopes. If it matches the conjunction family's alpha with a strong slope at 0.14 coverage it is the cleanest final answer, since it needs neither a cash-flow statement nor a second ranked leg.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Deal Outlays and Near-Term Debt Against the Equity Cushion
EXPRESSION: IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(TS_SUM(DELTA(ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), COALESCE(intan, 0)), 1), 5), dlc), SUB(at, lt)), 1))
HYPOTHESIS: The fragile firm is the one whose recent purchases of unverifiable intangible assets plus its debt maturing within the year are large relative to the book equity that must absorb any impairment, and this loss-absorption arithmetic is what the market underweights.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The archive's short-side constructs each captured one metric — the impairment overhang gave alpha −3.9% with ls_talpha −3.42 but a flat slope, the buy-versus-build conjunction gave fmb −4.50 with weaker alpha — because the former ignored maturing claims and the latter relied on a kinked conjunction. Combining recent deal outlays with short-term debt in the numerator and the equity cushion in the denominator states the fragility as one continuous solvency ratio, and winsorising handles the thin-equity tail that would otherwise dominate the ranking.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Build Minus Buy with Industry-Relative Earnings Floor
EXPRESSION: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), TS_SUM(DELTA(ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), COALESCE(intan, 0)), 1), 5)), at)), IND_RANK(TS_MIN(IND_ADJ(RATIO(ADD(ib, dp), at)), 5)))
HYPOTHESIS: The durability condition should be competitive rather than absolute: a firm qualifies if it out-earned its industry peers even in its worst year, which identifies a firm-specific moat supporting the research program rather than membership of a structurally profitable industry.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The industry-demeaned floor was tested only once, in gen 3, where it held up against the raw floor (fmb 4.24, alpha 3.8%, Sharpe 0.371) but was paired with a plain R&D-intensity leg and limited to the oancf sample; here it is combined with the strongest intangibles leg and the income-statement cash-earnings measure, extending it to roughly 0.13 coverage. This closes the run's central identification question — whether the repeated result is a moat effect or a residual industry-composition effect — while remaining a plausible top performer in its own right.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---CRITIQUE Horizon-Matched Build Minus Buy with Claims-Coverage Floor---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Internally coherent but essentially a mechanical re-pairing of two already-tested legs, with the gate swapped from a worst-year oancf/at floor to a near-collinear oancf/lct floor, so it is very likely a high-correlation near-duplicate of the gen-7 "Same-Horizon Build Minus Buy with Cash Floor" rather than a substantively new mechanism.

---CRITIQUE Intangible Allocation Per Dollar of Business Scale---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: A denominator change is a modest edit, but the stated purpose—testing whether the repeated build-minus-buy result is an asset-lightness/capital-intensity artefact rather than an allocation effect—is a legitimate identification test with a clear diagnostic payoff, and the expression matches the hypothesis.

---CRITIQUE Profit-Funded Knowledge Stock---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The construction genuinely embeds the earnings condition inside the accumulation in a way no archive leg does and the sign logic is consistent, but it sits close to the well-known R&D-capital-to-assets anomaly and will be highly correlated with the plain TS_SUM(xrd,5)/at leg since most firm-years are profitable, so the incremental content may be small.

---CRITIQUE Profit-Funded Knowledge Net of Deal Outlays---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: This is the previous proposal spliced onto the archive's already-tested "Net Durable Intangible Capital"/build-minus-buy numerator, so it is an incremental composite whose only new element is the profit indicator, and it imposes an arbitrary unit-for-unit netting of two heterogeneous dollar flows without justification.

---CRITIQUE Deal Outlays and Near-Term Debt Against the Equity Cushion---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: Dividing by book equity (at − lt) is internally inconsistent with the hypothesis because negative- or near-zero-equity firms—exactly the fragile cases the signal claims to identify—produce large negative or exploding ratios that rank as safest, and 1% winsorisation does not repair the sign flip.

---CRITIQUE Build Minus Buy with Industry-Relative Earnings Floor---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: A coherent conditional pairing that extends the industry-relative floor to the larger income-statement sample, though the claimed resolution of the moat-versus-industry-composition question is overstated since the outer IND_RANK already removes industry level and only the within-window ordering of the demeaned series adds new information.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Build Minus Buy with Worst-Year Cash Flow After Research
EXPRESSION: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), TS_SUM(DELTA(ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), COALESCE(intan, 0)), 1), 5)), at)), IND_RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(oancf, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 5)))
HYPOTHESIS: The binding condition for a research program is not that cash flow was positive but that cash flow was large enough to pay the research bill in the worst year: a firm whose operating cash flow net of research spending never went negative has an unconditionally self-financing innovation program.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: This is not a re-pairing of two archived legs because the quality gate itself now contains the intangibles variable — research spending is deducted from cash flow before the floor is taken — so the interaction operates inside both legs rather than only across them, and heavy researchers must clear a proportionately higher bar. The gen-2 attempt at self-funding used a count of qualifying years and failed on portfolio evidence (alpha −0.9%), whereas the magnitude form at the worst-year floor has never been tested and preserves the dispersion that a 0–5 count destroys.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Profit-Funded Research Under an Acquisitiveness Constraint
EXPRESSION: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(MUL(COALESCE(xrd, 0), INDICATOR(ib, 0)), 5), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(TS_SUM(DELTA(ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), COALESCE(intan, 0)), 1), 5), at))))
HYPOTHESIS: Two independent conditions define durable intangible productivity: research must have been financed out of profitable years, and the firm must not have been simultaneously buying intangible assets from outside; whichever condition binds determines the firm's credibility.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: Replacing the unit-for-unit netting with a weakest-link conjunction removes the arbitrary weighting the critic identified, since neither channel is forced onto the other's dollar scale and each enters as a separate constraint. The profit-weighted accumulation is the genuinely new element — the earnings test is applied year by year inside the knowledge stock rather than as a separate screen — and pairing it with the validated five-year acquisitiveness penalty keeps coverage near 0.14 with no cash-flow-statement requirement.

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Deal Outlays and Maturing Debt in Excess of Equity
EXPRESSION: IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(TS_SUM(DELTA(ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), COALESCE(intan, 0)), 1), 5), dlc), SUB(at, lt)), at))
HYPOTHESIS: A firm is fragile when its recent purchases of unverifiable intangible assets plus the debt maturing within the year exceed the book equity available to absorb an impairment, and the excess — not the ratio — is the economically meaningful quantity.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio
REASONING: Putting the equity cushion in the numerator as a subtraction and scaling everything by assets removes the sign pathology the critic identified: negative-equity firms now score at the fragile extreme rather than at the safe one, and the measure is monotone and defined for every firm. It follows the construction that already worked on the short side (the gen-5 impairment overhang, alpha −3.9% with ls_talpha −3.42) while adding the two elements that overhang omitted — recent deal outlays and near-term maturities — which the archive has separately shown to carry short-side information.
